facts.statement: The genus Dunhuangia was named and described in 2015 by Wang Min, Li Daqing, Jingmai Kathleen O'Connor, Zhou Zhonghe, and You Hailu.
facts.quote: In 2015, Wang Min, Li Daqing, Jingmai Kathleen O'Connor, Zhou Zhonghe and You Hailu named and described the type species Dunhuangia cuii.

facts.statement: The generic name Dunhuangia refers to the city of Dunhuang in Gansu province.
facts.quote: The generic name refers to the city of Dunhuang in Gansu province.

facts.statement: The specific name of the type species honors preparator Cui Guihia.
facts.quote: The specific name honours preparator Cui Guihia.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen GSGM-05-CM-030 was found in the Changma Basin within the Aptian-aged Xiagou Formation.
facts.quote: The holotype, GSGM-05-CM-030, was found in the Changma Basin, in a layer of the Xiagou Formation dating from the Aptian.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton that lacks the skull.
facts.quote: It consists of a partial skeleton lacking the skull.

facts.statement: The preserved skeleton includes the forelimbs, shoulder girdle, and sternum.
facts.quote: It contains the forelimbs, shoulder girdle and sternum.

facts.statement: Dunhuangia is classified as a medium-sized enantiornithean bird.
A unique feature of Dunhuangia is a pair of large notches on the rear edge of the sternum that equal over half the element's total length.
facts.quote: The rear edge of the sternum has a pair of large notches, equalling over half of the length of the entire element.

facts.statement: The coracoid bone features a deep trough on top bordered by a thick ridge that forms a vertically low outer bone wall.
facts.quote: The coracoid has a deep trough in the top, bordered on the outside by a thick ridge which forms the vertically low outer bone wall of the element.

facts.statement: Dunhuangia is classified within the Enantiornithes as the sister species to Fortunguavis.
facts.quote: Dunhuanagia was placed in the Enantiornithes, as sister species of Fortunguavis.

facts.statement: Dunhuangia lived during the Early Cretaceous in the area of present-day China.
facts.quote: Dunhuangia is a bird genus, belonging to the Enantiornithes, which during the Early Cretaceous lived in the area of present China.

facts.statement: The presence of Enantiornithes in the coastal Changma Basin is noted as unusual because these birds are typically arboreal.
facts.quote: This can be explained by the fact that the basin consists of coastal deposits while Enantiornithes are arboreal species.

facts.statement: Dunhuangia lived between 121.4 and 113.2 million years ago during the Aptian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (121.4 to 113.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Dunhuangia belongs to the subclass Enantiornithes.
The authority for the genus Dunhuangia is Wang et al., 2015.
Dunhuangia junchangi is a recognized type species within the genus.
Dunhuangia is an extinct avialan genus belonging to the Enantiornithes clade that inhabited China during the Early Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Dunhuangia es un género extinto de avialano perteneciente al clado Enantiornithes que habitó en el Cretácico inferior en lo que hoy es China.
